test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Priya can do a certain piece of work in 22 days. Priya and Varsha can together do the same work in 11 days, and Priya, Varsha and Nisha can do the same work together in 8 days. In how many days can Priya and Nisha do the same work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(22, 11, 8) = 88 units.

Efficiency of Priya = 88 ÷ 22 = 4 units/day.

Efficiency of Nisha = (Priya + Varsha + Nisha) − (Priya + Varsha) = (88 ÷ 8) − (88 ÷ 11) = 11 − 8 = 3 units/day.

Combined efficiency of Priya and Nisha = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day.

Time required by Priya and Nisha = 88 ÷ 7 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 88/7 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Priya = 22 days

Time taken by Priya and Varsha together = 11 days

Time taken by Priya, Varsha, and Nisha together = 8 days

**Method Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Nisha = (Efficiency of Priya, Varsha and Nisha) − (Efficiency of Priya and Varsha)

⇒ Efficiency of Nisha = 11 − 8 = 3 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of Priya and Nisha = Efficiency of Priya + Efficiency of Nisha

⇒ Combined efficiency = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day

⇒ Time taken by Priya and Nisha together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 88 ÷ 7 days

**∴ The correct answer is 88/7 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Works on the same concept as Time and Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, find the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days) and multiply by the maximum possible integer before calculating the remaining work manually.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each person. If they work for the same number of days, wages are directly proportional to their efficiencies.
